Two charts on a manifold, and their respective transition map

A transition map provides a way of comparing two charts of an atlas. To make this comparison, we consider the composition of one chart with the inverse of the other. This composition is not well-defined unless we restrict both charts to the intersection of their domains of definition. (For example, if we have a chart of Europe and a chart of Russia, then we can compare these two charts on their overlap, namely the European part of Russia.)

To be more precise, suppose that ${\displaystyle (U_{\alpha },\varphi _{\alpha })}$Image and ${\displaystyle (U_{\beta },\varphi _{\beta })}$Image are two charts for a manifold M such that ${\displaystyle U_{\alpha }\cap U_{\beta }}$Image is non-empty. The transition map ${\displaystyle \tau _{\alpha ,\beta }:\varphi _{\alpha }(U_{\alpha }\cap U_{\beta })\to \varphi _{\beta }(U_{\alpha }\cap U_{\beta })}$Image is the map defined by

    ${\displaystyle \tau _{\alpha ,\beta }=\varphi _{\beta }\circ \varphi _{\alpha }^{-1}.}$Image

Note that since ${\displaystyle \varphi _{\alpha }}$Image and ${\displaystyle \varphi _{\beta }}$Image are both homeomorphisms, the transition map ${\displaystyle \tau _{\alpha ,\beta }}$Image is also a homeomorphism.

This result, in particular, generalize Theorem 2.1 in [24] to arbitrary real analytic manifolds. Finally, we will show that, with the \(C^\nu\)-topology on the vector spaces \(C^\nu(N)\) and \(C^\nu(M)\), \(C^\nu\)-maps are continuous operators.

Let \(\phi : M \to N\) be a \(C^\nu\)-map. Then we can define the map \(\hat{\phi} : C^\nu(N) \to C^\nu(M)\) as

\[
\hat{\phi}(f)=f\circ \phi.
\]

It is easy to see that \(\hat{\phi}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-algebra homomorphism. For every \(x \in M\), one can define the unital \(\mathbb{F}\)-algebra homomorphism \(\mathrm{ev}_x : C^\nu(M) \to \mathbb{F}\) as

\[
\mathrm{ev}_x(f)=f(x).
\]

The map \(\mathrm{ev}_x\) is called the evaluation map at \(x \in M\). It is natural to ask whether the evaluation maps are continuous with respect to \(C^\nu\)-topology.

**Theorem 3.4.1.** *For every \(x \in M\), the map \(\mathrm{ev}_x : C^\nu(M) \to \mathbb{F}\) is continuous with respect to \(C^\nu\)-topology.*

*Proof.* If \(p_K^\nu\) is one of the seminorms \(p_{K,m}^{\infty}\), \(p_K^{\mathrm{phol}}\), or \(p_{K,a}^{\omega}\), we have

\[
p_K^\nu(f)\le C\,|\mathrm{ev}_x(f)|,
\]

where \(C=1\) for \(\nu\in\{\infty,\mathrm{hol}\}\) and \(C=a_0\) for \(\nu=\omega\). □
